name: Faxian
bio: Chinese Buddhist monk who travelled overland through Central Asia to India and returned by sea via Ceylon and Java (399-414 CE) to obtain authentic copies of the Vinaya (books of monastic discipline). His account is the earliest of the three and the shortest.

name: Xuanzang
bio: Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar and translator whose 16-year journey (629-645 CE) across Central Asia and the Indian subcontinent produced the most detailed surviving geographic record of ~110 'countries', studied at Nalanda, and brought back hundreds of texts. The most comprehensive of the three accounts.

source.work: The Great Tang Dynasty Record of the Western Regions

name: Yijing
bio: Chinese Buddhist monk who travelled to India by the maritime route via Srivijaya (Sumatra), studied at Nalanda, and spent years in Sribhoga (Palembang). His surviving work is a topical treatise on contemporary Indian monastic discipline rather than a place-by-place travelogue, but it is invaluable for the geographic distribution of the Buddhist schools.

source.work: A Record of the Buddhist Religion as Practised in India and the Malay Archipelago
